note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Memory-driven Intrinsic Cost Estimation (MICE): correcting cost-value underestimation to reduce constraint violations in CRL

nodes.name: CRL methods violate constraints in training
nodes.description: Existing CRL algorithms often exhibit persistent constraint violations during training, limiting their use in safety-critical scenarios.

nodes.name: Noise causes cost underestimation
nodes.description: Function-approximation noise breaks the zero-mean assumption under a minimization objective, causing underestimation of the cost value, so high-cost states appear deceptively safe (Fig 2).

nodes.name: Underestimation drives violations
nodes.description: Underestimating the cost value in high-cost regions leads agents to over-explore unsafe states and produces frequent constraint violations during training even when a safe optimal policy exists.

nodes.name: Bias can be useful if shaped
nodes.description: Underestimation encourages exploration and overestimation discourages it, so in high-cost regions overestimation helps prevent unsafe exploration, and the challenge is to shape the bias rather than remove it.

nodes.name: Flashbulb memory module
nodes.description: MICE stores previously explored unsafe states (positive extrinsic cost) from the previous iteration's policy, embedded by random projection, to identify high-cost regions.

nodes.name: Intrinsic cost as pseudo-count
nodes.description: The intrinsic cost is the kernel-similarity-based pseudo-count of the current state visiting high-cost regions in memory, normalized for stability.

nodes.name: Extrinsic-intrinsic cost value update
nodes.description: The extrinsic-intrinsic cost value function adds the intrinsic cost to the target, raising the cost estimate and mitigating underestimation in high-cost regions.

nodes.name: Balancing factor controls bias
nodes.description: A balancing intrinsic factor beta, updated from the previous update's estimated bias, raises the intrinsic cost when underestimating and lowers it when overestimating.

nodes.name: Trust-region objective keeps memory relevant
nodes.description: A trust-region objective keeps the updated policy close to the policy that generated the memory, so stored unsafe states stay relevant and the intrinsic cost reflects the updated policy's risk.

nodes.name: Constraint bounds and worst-case violation
nodes.description: The extrinsic-intrinsic cost admits constraint bounds (Theorem 4.3), and the MICE update has a worst-case constraint violation bound tighter than CPO's (Theorem 4.4).

nodes.name: Convergence guarantee
nodes.description: Under assumptions similar to TD3 and Double Q-learning, the extrinsic-intrinsic cost value function converges to the optimal Q_C (Theorem 4.5).

nodes.name: Reduces violations with comparable return
nodes.description: On Safety Gym and Safety MuJoCo, MICE significantly reduces constraint violations while maintaining policy performance similar or superior to baselines, matching Saute and SimmerPID's constraint satisfaction with better return (Figs 3-4).

nodes.name: MICE corrects estimation bias
nodes.description: Validation shows MICE mitigates underestimation, its estimation bias approaches zero, and its cost value converges to the true value (Fig 5).

nodes.name: Fixed intrinsic constants are worse
nodes.description: Replacing the memory-driven intrinsic cost with fixed constants (3, 5, 15) reduces return, and a larger constant (5 vs 3) does not necessarily reduce violations (Fig 6a,b).

nodes.name: Robust to thresholds
nodes.description: On SafetyPointGoal1-v0, MICE adapts to cost thresholds 0, 15 and 25, enforcing compliance even at threshold 0 (Fig 6c,d).

isolated_nodes.name: Experimental setup
isolated_nodes.description: Experiments run 10^7 steps, max trajectory length 1000, 6 seeds, on four Safety Gym navigation tasks and Safety MuJoCo with cost threshold 25.

isolated_nodes.name: Bias handling in prior RL
isolated_nodes.description: TD3, Double Q-learning and AdaEQ address overestimation, while Maxmin and Balanced Q-learning show estimation bias can be controlled to enhance learning.

isolated_nodes.name: Random projection cheapens computation
isolated_nodes.description: Ablation of the random projection layer shows it significantly reduces computational complexity without degrading performance or increasing violations (Appendix C.3.4).

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from the underestimation diagnosis, through the flashbulb memory and intrinsic cost design, to the trust-region update with theoretical guarantees, then experimental validation.
